1. This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for claiming compensation on account of death of Faras.S., S/o Late Mohan Kumar.

2. It is the case of the petitioners that on 27-06-2023 at about 2-00 a.m., within the jurisdiction of Pulakeshinagara Traffic Police Station, at Lazar road when the deceased Sri.S.Usuf Khan was riding the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.TN-05-BK- 4251 along with deceased Sri. Faras.S as pillion rider from M.M. Road Mask Circle towards Police station circle, at that time the driver/accused/Sunil Babu Rathod of the offending Tipper vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AC-2837 drove the said vehicle from Budhavihara road towards Lazar road - MM road Junction in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/deceased of the unoffending vehicle fell down on the road and the wheel of the offending vehicle run over the deceased rider, pillion rider and unoffending vehicle, as a result the Parvathi Devi vs Velu M on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178682319/
2 unoffending vehicle seriously damaged and the rider and the pillion rider/Faras.S were sustained grievous bleeding injuries and died at the spot.
Thereafter, the informant/Abdul Wajid lodged complaint before the 4 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 Pulakeshinagara Traffic police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.105/2023 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279 and 304A of IPC R/w Section 115 and 177 of IMV Act and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
3.

It is contended that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioners No.2 is the sister and Petitioner No.3 is the brother of the deceased Sri.Faras.S., and as on the date of the alleged accident the said deceased was aged about 19 years and he was working as Supplier at the Grand Hyderabadi Biriyani and earning income Rs.25,000/- p.m., and Rs.500/- per day as tips.
The petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- under different head of loss of dependency, funeral and obsequies expenses, loss of filial love, loss of consortium, loss of estate.

4 It is contended that the accident is solely due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04/AC-2837 and the respondent No.1 is the RC owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 is placed exparte and the Respondent No.2 has appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement.

6. In the written statement of Respondent No.2 Insurance Company, it has admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioners have not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further it is denied having insured the vehicle involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the deceased.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioners have constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of 6 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V.Act.
Hence sought for dismissal of the petition.

It is contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle.

The Respondent No.2/ Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the deceased and the said deceased crossed the road on taking note of the approaching offending vehicle and the driver of the offending vehicle cannot save accident,
however, slowly he may be riding and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

13.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioners.

Hence, in order to prove their case,
the Petitioner No.1 herself examined as P.W.1 and she has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in her evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.14 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex .P-1 is the True copy of FIR, Ex.P-2 is the copy of Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the MVA Report, Ex.P.6 is the Inquest report, Ex.P.7 is the Postmortem report, Ex.P.8 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P.9 is the Notice issued under Section 133 of MV Act to the owner of the offending vehicle,
Ex.P.10 is the Reply to the notice given by the owner of the offending vehicle, Ex.P.11 is the Adhar Card of Parvathi Devi, Ex.P.12 is the Adhar Card of Laxmi Maya, Ex.P.13 is the Adhar Card of Babun and Ex.P.14 is the Death Certificate.
In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the Respondent No.2 she has deposed that the deceased is her son and at the time of accident the deceased was proceeding in the Motor Cycle as a pillion rider.
She has not seen the alleged accident.
Further she has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to fault and negligence riding of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the offending vehicle.
Further she denied that she has not incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards funeral expenditure of his son.
Further she denied that her son was not working and not earning income as alleged.
Further she has denied that the Petitioners are not dependent on the income of the deceased.
Further she has denied that in order to get more compensation she has deposing that they are residing with the deceased and depending on the income of the deceased.

Further she has denied that in order to get more compensation in collusion with the police they have falsely implicated the offending vehicle and filed false case against the offending vehicle and produced concocted created documents and filed false affidavit and deposing falsely.

During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and he has made those 11 SCCH - 7 Parvathi Devi vs Velu M on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178682319/
5 MVC.No.8374/2023 versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

sentences.text: 15. On careful reading of Ex.P5/MVA report it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending vehicle.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, back side left wheel mudguard scratched.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the unoffending vehicle and opined that, front full body damaged, both head light damaged and back engine cover damaged.

16. On going through the Ex.P-7/Postmortem report it is seen that Doctor opined that cause of death of deceased is due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained in the alleged road traffic accident.

17. On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint on 27.06.2023, the police have visited the spot and the informant/complainant has shown the spot and the police have conducted the detailed spot mahazar, in the presence of panch witnesses and during the mahazar the police have prepared Ex.P.4/Spot Sketch therein.

On going through the Ex.P-2/ Complaint it is seen that on 27-06-2023 at about 2-00 a.m.,
within the jurisdiction of Pulakeshinagara Traffic Police Station, at Lazar road when the deceased Sri.S.Usuf Khan was riding the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.TN- 05-BK-4251 along with deceased Sri. Faras.S as pillion rider from M.M. Road Mask Circle towards Police station circle,
at that time the driver/accused/Sunil Babu Rathod of the offending Tipper vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-AC-2837 drove the said vehicle from Budhavihara road towards Lazar road - MM road Junction in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/deceased of the unoffending vehicle fell down on the road and the wheel of the offending vehicle run over the deceased rider, pillion rider and unoffending vehicle, as a result the unoffending vehicle seriously damaged and the rider and the pillion rider/Faras.S were sustained grievous bleeding injuries and died at the spot.
The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

19. The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and 13 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 counsel further contended that the offending vehicle was moving slowly and the deceased suddenly crossed the road at the spot on taking note of the approaching offending vehicle and due to his fault the alleged accident occurred.

The alleged accident occurred due to no fault of the accused and the driver of the offending vehicle cannot save accident, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
20.

Admittedly, the accused is the rider of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, deceased was dead due to grievous injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, MVA Report, Inquest mahazar, Postmortem report and Charge Sheet and the evidence of Parvathi Devi vs Velu M on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178682319/
6 PW-1 are specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly 14 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the deceased Faras.S., as a result he sustained grievous injuries and died due to alleged accident.
In view of the police records, it clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the deceased Faras.S., S/o Late Mohan Kumar died due to injuries sustained in the alleged accident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Faras.S., S/o Late Mohan Kumar noted in the Ex.P7/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the 15 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 offences punishable under sections 279, 304A of IPC R/w Section 115 and 177 of IMV Act.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent teenage boy Sri.Faras.S., S/o Late Mohan Kumar aforesaid, as the driver of offending vehicle/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.

Therefore,
the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2 to 4:-

The Learned Counsel for the Petitioners contended that the deceased was aged about 19 years at the time of accident and he was working as Supplier at the Grand Hyderabadi Biriyani and earning income Rs.25,000/- p.m., and Rs.500/- per day as tips.
The Petitioner No.1 is mother, Petitioner No.2 is the sister and Petitioner No.3 is the brother of the deceased.

Further the Counsel contended that as per the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, the Petitioners being legal heirs and dependents of deceased, each of the Petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head 16 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 of loss of love and affection consortium and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.
22.

sentences.text: On going through the Ex.P-11 to Ex.P.13/Adhar Cards of the Petitioners and Ex.P-14/death certificate of the deceased
, it is seen that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioner No.2 is the sister and Petitioner No.3 is the brother of the deceased.
Hence on the strength of Ex.P-11 to Ex.P.13/Adhar Cards and Ex.P-14 it is crystal clear that the Petitioners are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased.

24. The petitioners have contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 19 years and he was working as Supplier at the Grand Hyderabadi Biriyani, and earning income Rs.25,000/- p.m., and Rs.500/- per day as tips.
The petitioners relied on the Ex.P-7/Postmortem report of the deceased, wherein the age of the deceased is shown as 19 years.
Hence it is 17 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 clear that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 19 years.

Hence the age of the deceased is considered as 19 years.
25.
It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
In the instance case the petitioners claimed that deceased was was working as Supplier at the Grand Hyderabadi Biriyani, and earning income Rs.25,000/- p.m., and Rs.500/- per day as tips.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the actual income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the deceased taken at Rs.15,250/-.

The Petitioners No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of the deceased, in view of the law laid down by the constitution bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.

sentences.text:
Thus the 40% of the future prospects is to be added,
hence the monthly income comes to Rs.21,350/- (Rs.15,250/- + 40%).

Since the deceased is the bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% towards personal and living expenses and 18 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 remaining amount, i.e., Rs.10,675/- (Rs.21,350/- - Rs.10,675/-) has to be taken as his/deceased contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 19 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.
Thus the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.23,05,800/- (Rs.10,675/- x 12 x 18) on account of loss of dependency.
26. In addition, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioner No.2 is the sister and Petitioner No.3 is the brother of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.

Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to the deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 and 4 partly in the affirmative and Issue No.3 in the Affirmative.

30. Issue No.5: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
20 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.26,05,800/- (Rupees Twenty Six lakhs Five Thousand and Eight Hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of total compensation amount, the Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 60% share with interest and the Petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for 20% share each with interest.
After deposit, entire share of compensation amount with interest allotted to the Petitioner No.1 shall be released in her favour through E- payment with proper verification and identification.
The entire shares of the petitioners No.2 and 3 shall be kept as FD till they attains the age of majority.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

3 (1) Whether the Petitioners proves that deceased Faras.S. S/o Late Mohan Kumar sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of driving of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AC-2837 on dated 27-06-2023 at about 2-00 p.m., and succumbed to injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioners proves the age and earning of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Faras.S S/o Late Mohan Kumar?
(4) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum? from whom?
( 5) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Respondent No.2/ Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the deceased and the said deceased crossed the road on taking note of the approaching offending vehicle and the driver of the offending vehicle cannot save accident,
however, slowly he may be riding and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Since the Petitioners have not established the income of the deceased, they are not entitled for compensation towards future prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the deceased Faras.S., as a result he sustained grievous injuries and died due to alleged accident.
In view of the police records, it clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the 15 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 offences punishable under sections 279, 304A of IPC R/w Section 115 and 177 of IMV Act.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent teenage boy Sri.Faras.S., S/o Late Mohan Kumar aforesaid, as the driver of offending vehicle/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore,
the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
24. The petitioners have contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 19 years and he was working as Supplier at the Grand Hyderabadi Biriyani, and earning income Rs.25,000/- p.m., and Rs.500/- per day as tips.
The petitioners relied on the Ex.P-7/Postmortem report of the deceased, wherein the age of the deceased is shown as 19 years.
Hence the age of the deceased is considered as 19 years.
25.
It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
In the instance case the petitioners claimed that deceased was was working as Supplier at the Grand Hyderabadi Biriyani, and earning income Rs.25,000/- p.m., and Rs.500/- per day as tips.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the actual income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the deceased taken at Rs.15,250/-.
The Petitioners No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of the deceased, in view of the law laid down by the constitution bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus the 40% of the future prospects is to be added,
hence the monthly income comes to Rs.21,350/- (Rs.15,250/- + 40%).
Since the deceased is the bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% towards personal and living expenses and 18 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 remaining amount, i.e., Rs.10,675/- (Rs.21,350/- - Rs.10,675/-) has to be taken as his/deceased contribution to the family.
Thus the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.23,05,800/- (Rs.10,675/- x 12 x 18) on account of loss of dependency.
26. In addition, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.
In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioner No.2 is the sister and Petitioner No.3 is the brother of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.
Thus the Petitioners are entitled to the following compensation:
27.
The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
19 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 Sl.No. Compensation under Amount in (Rs)
different heads 1 Loss of dependency 23,05,800.00 2 Funeral Expenses 15,000.00 3 Loss of Estate 15,000.00 4 Loss of filial consortium 1,20,000.00 5 Loss of love and affection 1,50,000.00
Total 26,05,800.00
The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.26,05,800/-.
29.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to the deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 and 4 partly in the affirmative and Issue No.3 in the Affirmative.
30. Issue No.5: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
20 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8374/2023 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.26,05,800/- (Rupees Twenty Six lakhs Five Thousand and Eight Hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of total compensation amount, the Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 60% share with interest and the Petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for 20% share each with interest.
After deposit, entire share of compensation amount with interest allotted to the Petitioner No.1 shall be released in her favour through E- payment with proper verification and identification.
The entire shares of the petitioners No.2 and 3 shall be kept as FD till they attains the age of majority.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
